questions.title: Section A: Multiple Choice, Matching, Terminology and True/False

subQuestions.questionText: The … in fowl is responsible for the physical digestion.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - ventriculus (2 marks)
The ventriculus (gizzard) in fowl is responsible for the physical/mechanical digestion of food.

subQuestions.questionText: Lipase is an enzyme that helps to break down fat into …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - glycerol and fatty acids (2 marks)
Lipase breaks down fats/lipids into glycerol and fatty acids.

subQuestions.questionText:
It is important to feed roughage to a fully grown ruminant because it:
(i) Prevents the accumulation of gases when grazing on lucerne
(ii) Stimulates the development of the rumen
(iii) Supplies bulkiness to the ration
(iv) Ensures that digestion takes place properly
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - (i), (iii) and (iv) (2 marks)
For a fully grown ruminant, roughage prevents bloat (gas accumulation), supplies bulk and ensures proper digestion. Rumen development (ii) applies to young ruminants, not fully grown.

subQuestions.questionText: In a cafeteria style, farm animals are allowed to …
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - take minerals according to their individual needs (2 marks)
Cafeteria-style feeding allows animals to self-select minerals based on their individual needs.

options.A: eat less minerals than they require.
options.C: eat more minerals than they require.
options.D: take minerals according to their individual needs.

subQuestions.questionText: The picture below illustrates ... as a reason for handling farm animals. (Refer to picture in question paper showing tail-related procedure.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D - docking (2 marks)
The picture shows docking, which is the removal of part of the tail.

subQuestions.questionText: The purpose of vaccination is mainly to … diseases in farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - prevent (2 marks)
Vaccination is a preventative measure that stimulates immunity to prevent disease.

subQuestions.questionText:
The following statements are TRUE with regard to the use of foldable curtains in a broiler house:
(i) The effect of environmental temperature is controlled.
(ii) Efficient feed utilisation can be achieved.
(iii) It darkens the broiler house to increase feed consumption.
(iv) It is a necessary feature to reduce the effect of heat stress.
Choose the CORRECT combination:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B - (i), (ii) and (iv) (2 marks)
Foldable curtains control environmental temperature, allow efficient feed utilisation and reduce heat stress. They do not darken the house (statement iii is incorrect).

subQuestions.questionText: Which ONE of the following combinations of diseases is classified as proclaimed viral diseases?
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Rabies and foot-and-mouth disease (2 marks)
Both rabies and foot-and-mouth disease are proclaimed viral diseases. Anthrax and tuberculosis are bacterial.

subQuestions.questionText: … are the congenital defects in bulls leading to sterility.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C - Hypoplasia and hermaphroditism (2 marks)
Hypoplasia (underdevelopment of testes) and hermaphroditism are congenital defects causing sterility in bulls.

subQuestions.questionText: The accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid in the brain of a foetus leading to difficult parturition:
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A - Hydrocephalus (2 marks)
Hydrocephalus is the accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid in the brain causing difficult parturition.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE: A non-protein nitrogen substance that is safer to use because it is less soluble. (A: Urea; B: Biuret)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B only (2 marks)
Biuret is a non-protein nitrogen substance that is safer than urea because it is less soluble.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE: Feed containing a lot of protein with a high biological value. (A: NR 1 : 4; B: NR 1 : 7)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: A only (2 marks)
A narrow nutritive ratio (NR 1:4) indicates a feed high in protein with high biological value.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE: Chemical method to control parasites. (A: Dipping; B: Dosing)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Both A and B (2 marks)
Both dipping (for external parasites) and dosing (for internal parasites) are chemical methods of controlling parasites.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE: A system of keeping each layer in her own small wire cage for the entire productive cycle. (A: Backyard; B: Deep litter)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: None (2 marks)
The description refers to the battery cage system, not backyard or deep litter systems.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE: Hormone preventing the growth and ripening of the Graafian follicle. (A: Follicle stimulating hormone (FSH); B: Progesterone)
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: B only (2 marks)
Progesterone prevents the growth and ripening of the Graafian follicle (FSH stimulates it).

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The type of animal feed that contains a small volume per unit mass.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Concentrate (2 marks)
Concentrates are feeds with high nutrient density and small volume per unit mass.

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: A permanent handling facility used to restrict the movement of a bull and lead it towards a loading ramp.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Crush / crush pen / race (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The process in lactating cows that is stimulated by hormones resulting in the flow of milk.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Milk let down / milk ejection (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The cell that fuses with the ovum during the process of fertilisation.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Sperm cell / spermatozoon / male gamete / male sex cell (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE word/term: The transfer of a fertilised ovum from one cow to another.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Embryo transfer / transplant / ET (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: Tranquilisers stimulate the growth of farm animals by causing the secretion of a thyroxin hormone.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Thyroid regulators (1 mark)
Thyroid regulators (not tranquilisers) stimulate growth via thyroxin secretion.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: Cleaning is the application of chemicals to create an environment free from disease-causing micro-organisms.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Disinfecting / sanitising (1 mark)
Disinfecting (not cleaning) involves chemicals to kill disease-causing micro-organisms.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: The ovum phase is characterised by cell differentiation into tissues, organs and systems.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Embryonic (1 mark)
The embryonic phase (not ovum phase) is characterised by cell differentiation into tissues, organs and systems.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: Fertilisation is the process where female animals in a herd are made to come into oestrus simultaneously.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Synchronisation of oestrus (1 mark)
Synchronisation of oestrus (not fertilisation) is the process of making females come into oestrus simultaneously.

subQuestions.questionText: Change the UNDERLINED WORD to make the statement TRUE: The epididymis is responsible for the production of the male sex hormone in bulls.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Testis (1 mark)
The testis (not the epididymis) produces the male sex hormone (testosterone).

subQuestions.questionText: The diagram shows the alimentary canal of a farm animal (with parts A, B, C, D, E, ileum, caecum, rectum). Name the farm animal whose alimentary canal is represented in the diagram above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Pig (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the diagram to motivate the answer to QUESTION 2.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: The animal has a simple/single/monogastric stomach (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Physical and chemical digestion in the alimentary canal of the farm animal named in QUESTION 2.1.1 takes place in the mouth. Justify this statement.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Physical - Food is broken down by the teeth into smaller particles (1 mark)
Mark 2: Chemical - Salivary amylase in the mouth breaks down starch in food into maltose (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify, in the diagram above, the part where EACH of the following occurs (write only the letter):
(a) Soluble food particles move into the blood
(b) Soluble caseinogen in milk is changed into insoluble casein
(c) Bile is produced
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) B (1 mark) - small intestine, where absorption occurs
(b) D (1 mark) - stomach, where caseinogen is converted to casein by rennin
(c) A (1 mark) - liver, which produces bile

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the part in the alimentary canal of ruminant farm animals that corresponds to D in the diagram above in terms of functioning.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Abomasum (1 mark)
The abomasum is the 'true stomach' of ruminants, equivalent to the monogastric stomach (D).

subQuestions.questionText: The flow chart shows components of feed: Feed → A and Dry matter; Dry matter → Inorganic (Phosphorus, Iron, Zinc) and Organic (Vit. K, Vit. B1). State TWO roles of component A (water/moisture) in digestion of farm animals.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Acts as a solvent for dissolving substances in the body
• Softens/moistens food
• Facilitating enzymatic digestion
• Medium through which waste products are excreted
• Transports nutrients through the digestive tract

subQuestions.questionText:
Identify the component in the flow chart above that will result in the following deficiency symptoms:
(a) Slow healing of wounds in farm animals
(b) Excessive bleeding in chickens
(c) Chewing of dry bones by farm animals
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Zinc (1 mark) - zinc deficiency causes slow wound healing
(b) Vitamin K (1 mark) - vitamin K deficiency causes excessive bleeding (clotting failure)
(c) Phosphorus (1 mark) - phosphorus deficiency causes pica/bone chewing

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the organic component in the flow chart above that is:
(a) Fat soluble
(b) Water soluble
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Fat soluble - Vitamin K (1 mark)
(b) Water soluble - Vitamin B1 (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: In a feed digestibility trial, two ruminant animals were each given 12 kg of dry feed. Animal A: dry mass of manure = 2 kg, digestibility coefficient = 83%. Animal B: dry mass of manure = 7 kg, digestibility coefficient = ?. Calculate the digestibility coefficient of the feed in ANIMAL B. Include the formula.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: $DC = \frac{\text{Dry material intake (kg)} - \text{Dry mass of manure (kg)}}{\text{Dry material intake (kg)}} \times 100$ (1 mark)
Mark 2: Substitution: $= \frac{12 - 7}{12} \times 100$ (1 mark)
Mark 3: Calculation: $= \frac{5}{12} \times 100$ (1 mark)
Mark 4: Answer: $= 41{,}6\%$ or $42\%$ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce TWO animal related factors that might have influenced the digestibility of the feed given to ANIMAL A and ANIMAL B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Individuality
• Age of animal
• Production

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO methods by which to increase the digestibility of the feed in ANIMAL B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Grinding/milling
• Pelleting
• Boiling
• Crushing
• Soaking
• Popping and micronizing
• Dry rolling and cracking
• Roasting
• Mixing with molasses
• Cutting hay at an early stage

subQuestions.questionText: A lamb was given a feed containing 50% total digestible nutrients and 5% digestible protein. Calculate the nutritive ratio (NR) of this feed.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Formula: $NR = 1 : \frac{\%TDN - \%DP}{\%DP}$ (1 mark)
Mark 2: Substitution: $= 1 : \frac{50 - 5}{5} = 1 : \frac{45}{5}$ (1 mark)
Mark 3: Answer: $= 1 : 9$ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Based on the calculated nutritive ratio in QUESTION 2.4.1, indicate the suitability of this feed for its intended purpose.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Suitable for fattening / not suitable for growth/production (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 2.4.2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Less protein
• NR is wide / more carbohydrates than protein

subQuestions.questionText: Classify this feed that was given to the lamb.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Roughage (1 mark)
A feed with a wide nutritive ratio (1:9) is classified as roughage.

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE advantage of feeding the lamb with the feed in QUESTION 2.4.4.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• To stimulate the development of the rumen
• Adds volume required for ruminant digestion

subQuestions.questionText: The fodder flow programme table shows: 50 animals over 6 months; in month 6, requirement = 9,5 kg/animal/day. Calculate the total amount of feed required (in tons) by the animals in month 6.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Calculation: $9{,}5 \text{ kg} \times 50 \text{ animals} \times 30 \text{ days} = 14{,}250 \text{ kg}$ (1 mark)
Mark 2: Conversion: $\frac{14{,}250 \text{ kg}}{1000} $ (1 mark)
Mark 3: Answer: $= 14{,}25 \text{ tons}$ (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Deduce the problem in the fodder flow programme above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Shortage / deficit of feed during month 5/6 (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a reason for your answer to QUESTION 2.5.2 based on the table.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Supply is 12 tons in month 5 and 4 tons in month 6 while the requirement is 13,5 and 14,25 tons respectively / feed available is less than feed required (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The picture shows an animal production system (livestock on natural veld with vast space). Identify the production system shown in the picture above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Extensive (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons, based on the picture above, to justify the answer to QUESTION 3.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Kept on a natural veld
• Unit area is vast per animal / large space, fewer animals
• Lack of shelter/protection
• Animals fend for themselves

subQuestions.questionText:
Compare the TWO production systems used in livestock enterprises based on the following:
(a) Production output per unit area
(b) Disease transmission
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Production output per unit area (2 marks):
• Intensive: High (1 mark)
• Extensive: Low (1 mark)

(b) Disease transmission (2 marks):
• Intensive: High (1 mark)
• Extensive: Less (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The pictures show pieces of equipment (A: burdizzo/castrator; B: syringe; C: shears; D: branding iron; E: drench gun) used for handling techniques. Match equipment (A–E) above with the handling techniques ((a)–(e)) below:
(a) Crutching the wool in the wet areas around the tail
(b) Branding of cattle
(c) Castration of older calves
(d) Oral administration of worm remedies
(e) Intravenous administration of medicines
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) C (shears) (1 mark)
(b) D (branding iron) (1 mark)
(c) A (burdizzo/castrator) (1 mark)
(d) E (drench gun) (1 mark)
(e) B (syringe) (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons for handling cattle, other than the ones indicated in QUESTION 3.2.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Transportation
• General examination
• Pregnancy diagnosis
• Weighing
• Control external parasites/dipping/foot bathing
• Age determination
• Dehorning
• Hoof trimming
• Artificial insemination
• Production purposes
• Slaughtering
• Selection
• Weaning
• Feeding
• Docking
• Evaluation and classification
• Generation of data

subQuestions.questionText: The picture shows a certain behaviour in farm animals (cattle pushing/aggressive). Identify the behaviour shown by farm animals above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Fright / frightened / animals scared
• Aggression
• Pushing

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate the cause of the following farm animal behaviour:
(a) Cattle refusing to get into the plunge dip
(b) Chicks moving away from each other with open beaks and rapid breathing
(c) Sheep turning disorderly and not easy to handle individually
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Poor depth perception (1 mark)
(b) Heat stress (1 mark)
(c) Flocking habit (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Refer to the bar graph showing blowflies strike in ewes and lambs over months May to October. Classify the type of parasite illustrated in the graph above.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Ecto / external parasites (1 mark)
Blowflies are external parasites that attack the surface of the animal's body.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the month with the highest blowfly infestation.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: September (1 mark)
The combined ewe and lamb infestation peaks in September (8 ewes + 10 lambs = 18 strikes/1000).

subQuestions.questionText:
Deduce the rate of infestation by the blowfly in both ewes and lambs during the months of:
(a) May
(b) August
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) May - Ewes are more infested than lambs / 4 000 ewes and 1 000 lambs (1 mark)
(b) August - Ewes are less infested than lambs / 6 000 ewes and 8 000 lambs (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State a financial implication for the farmer if the blowfly infestation is allowed to rise.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Loss of production/stock
• Loss of profit/income / high costs of treatment

subQuestions.questionText: State ONE preventative measure by wool sheep farmers to reduce the impact of this parasite.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Shear whilst still cool for the blowfly not to survive / correct time of shearing
• Docking of the tails
• Treat diarrhoea
• Avoid/treat open wounds
• Separate rams to avoid fighting
• Crutching of wet soiled areas
• Controlling of flies
• Breeding resistant animals

subQuestions.questionText: The flow chart shows different farm animal diseases (A: Proclaimed disease causing persistent cough; B: Bloodstained nasal discharge transmitted by ticks; C: Aggressiveness, excessive salivating, transmissible to humans; D: viral; E: viral, hot/wet seasons). Identify the pathogen responsible for diseases A and B.
subQuestions.memoText:
A - Bacteria (1 mark) - persistent cough is characteristic of bacterial diseases like tuberculosis
B - Protozoon (1 mark) - tick-borne disease with bloodstained nasal discharge (e.g. redwater) is caused by protozoa

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate the transmission mode of the virus for disease D.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Infected saliva through biting (1 mark)
This is the transmission mode for rabies (described in C of the chart - aggressiveness, excessive salivation, transmissible to humans).

subQuestions.questionText: Name the vector that carries viral disease E during hot, wet seasons.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Mosquitoes (1 mark)
Mosquitoes are vectors for diseases like Rift Valley Fever during hot, wet seasons.

subQuestions.questionText: Advise the farmer on a preventative measure for the occurrence of disease E.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Destroy the vector at the breeding place / spraying / destroy infected animals
• Vaccination
• Isolation
• Awareness campaigns

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO measures the state can take to control the spread of disease C, once detected.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Culling/killing of infected animals
• Eradication programs set into place
• Quarantining/isolation
• Import and export bans

subQuestions.questionText: Poisoning is common in farm animals that are deprived of fresh, clean water while being exposed to diets high in sodium chloride. Name the type of poisoning referred to in the statement above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Salt poisoning (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the mineral source of the poisoning from the statement above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Sodium chloride / NaCl (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE treatment measure if animals get this form of poisoning.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Removal of the source of salts
• Provision of fresh clean water in smaller quantities
• Supplying water through a stomach tube for severe cases
• Treating animals with hypertonic dextrose / isotonic / saline solution

subQuestions.questionText: State a preventative measure for this form of poisoning.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Supply clean fresh water
• Do not deprive animals of salt for too long / avoid craving for salt
• Supply acceptable quantities of salt / no free access to abundant supply of salt

subQuestions.questionText: The diagrams illustrate the reproductive systems of cattle (Diagram A with parts A, B, C, D; Diagram B with parts E, F, G, H). Identify the diagram (A or B) above that represents the reproductive system of a cow.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Diagram A (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE visible reason in the diagram for the answer to QUESTION 4.1.1.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any 1 of the following (1 mark):
• Presence of an ovary
• Presence of uterus
• Presence of cervix
• Presence of vagina
• Presence of fallopian tube

subQuestions.questionText: Name parts C and G.
subQuestions.memoText:
C - Cervix (1 mark)
G - Cowper's / bulbo-urethral glands (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give a function of EACH of the following:
(a) Part B
(b) The fluid secreted by part F
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Part B - Where the zygote is implanted and develops (1 mark)
(b) Part F (any 1, 1 mark):
• Fluid provides nutrients to the sperm cells
• Protect semen against pH changes
• Helps to keep semen fertile and healthy
• Improves mobility of the spermatozoa

subQuestions.questionText: Identify the letter representing the part where gametes are formed in DIAGRAM B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: E (1 mark)
E represents the testis, where male gametes (sperm) are formed.

subQuestions.questionText:
Mating is a natural process that occurs in stages. The list of stages provided is:
• Semen is released into the vagina.
• A bull gains intromission into the vagina.
• A bull shows interest in a cow.
• A bull stands on his rear legs and rests on the rear end of the cow.
Rearrange the stages of mating above in their chronological order.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct chronological order (1 mark each):
1. A bull shows interest in a cow
2. A bull stands on his rear legs and rests on the rear end of the cow
3. A bull gains intromission into the vagina
4. Semen is released into the vagina

subQuestions.questionText: State the stage NOT indicated above.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Dismounting (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the hormone that regulates the mating behaviour in bulls.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Testosterone (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText:
The graph shows the levels of ovarian hormones in a cow over 30 days, with two lines (A and B). Curve B peaks around day 14 then drops; curve A rises from day 16 onwards and stabilises. Identify the letter (A or B) representing the following hormones:
(a) Oestrogen
(b) Progesterone
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Oestrogen - B (1 mark)
Oestrogen peaks around oestrus (day 14) and then declines.

(b) Progesterone - A (1 mark)
Progesterone rises after ovulation and is maintained during pregnancy.

subQuestions.questionText:
Name the stage in the oestrus cycle:
(a) Between day 2 and day 6
(b) At day 14
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Between day 2 and 6 - Pro-oestrus (1 mark)
(b) At day 14 - Oestrus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The cow fell pregnant on day 16. Refer to the hormonal levels to justify this statement.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Oestrogen level dropped (1 mark)
Mark 2: Progesterone level is increasing and maintained (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the stage in a normal reproductive cycle of a cow 282 days after insemination.
subQuestions.memoText:
Answer: Parturition / calving (1 mark)
The gestation period of a cow is approximately 282 days.

subQuestions.questionText:
The table shows the milk yield of two groups of lactating cows over 25 weeks:
Week 5: Group 1 = 10 L, Group 2 = 13 L
Week 10: Group 1 = 25 L, Group 2 = 16 L
Week 15: Group 1 = 15 L, Group 2 = 18 L
Week 20: Group 1 = 13 L, Group 2 = 20 L
Week 25: Group 1 = 10 L, Group 2 = 20 L
Draw a bar graph showing the milk yield of the two groups of lactating cows.
subQuestions.memoText:
Bar graph showing milk yield of two groups of lactating cows over a period of 25 weeks.

MARKING CRITERIA (1 mark each):
• Correct heading (e.g. 'Milk yield of two groups of lactating cows over a period of 25 weeks')
• X-axis: Correctly calibrated with label (Time)
• Y-axis: Correctly calibrated with label (Milk yield)
• Correct units (litres and weeks)
• Combined bar graph format
• Accuracy of bars

Values to plot:
• Week 5: Group 1 = 10 L, Group 2 = 13 L
• Week 10: Group 1 = 25 L, Group 2 = 16 L
• Week 15: Group 1 = 15 L, Group 2 = 18 L
• Week 20: Group 1 = 13 L, Group 2 = 20 L
• Week 25: Group 1 = 10 L, Group 2 = 20 L

subQuestions.questionText: Compare the milk yield in both groups over the weeks.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Group 1 - Milk yield increased and then it decreased (1 mark)
Mark 2: Group 2 - Milk yield increased and then it stabilised (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The equipment/apparatus used during artificial insemination (AI) is shown (Picture A: AI straws/insemination guns; Picture B: liquid nitrogen storage flasks). State the function of the apparatus in PICTURE A and the equipment in PICTURE B during AI.
subQuestions.memoText:
Picture A - Depositing semen into the reproductive tracts of a cow (1 mark)
Picture B - Storage of semen (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the reproductive part where the apparatus in PICTURE A is placed during AI.
subQuestions.memoText: Answer: Cervix / uterus (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO basic requirements when the equipment in PICTURE B is used.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Semen be stored at 5 °C for shorter periods
• Semen stored for longer periods must be frozen in liquid nitrogen at -196 °C
• Semen must be stored in polyvinyl straws
• End of straws be sealed to prevent entering of liquid nitrogen
• Straws be labelled for identification

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO challenges of using the equipment in PICTURE B.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO of the following (1 mark each):
• Expensive
• Needs expert knowledge on how to handle
• Correct handling and maintenance
